- `frontend/` contains a simple Svelte application
- `ingest/` contains the legacy Python scripts used to bootstrap this project.

## Exposed coding policy

- Follow with strict detail to the existing style of the application. This includes:
  - Type driven design
  - Domain modelling and parse-not-validate
  - Consistent error handling
  - Service layer abstractions

- Interactions with the database must use `sqlx` macros for compile-time query verification.

  [Rust domain development skill](.agents/skills/rust-domain-development/SKILL.md).

  retain typed values internally.

  depends on a variant.

  than synchronizing the copies. Trace changes through producers, serialization,
  consumers, and persistence together.

## Frontend coding policy

- The frontend is largely in a prototype stage so changes can be made freely without much guidance.

  its description. Capture the affected views from the running application on
  the PR branch after completing the changes.

  `gh pr edit --attach`. Use a GitHub CLI version that supports this flag. Never
  commit PR screenshots to the repository. Verify that the attachments render
  in the PR description before marking the PR ready for review.


## Ingest coding policy

- When porting code from this project, do not replicate the style. Use it as an end to end guide for functionality.

## Worktree policy

- For read-only tasks (investigating, reading, summarizing, or describing code),
  work on the current branch without creating a worktree.

  worktree before making changes. If a read-only task expands to require changes,
  switch to a dedicated worktree first.
- For such changes, reuse this chat's dedicated worktree if one already exists.
  Otherwise, create a sibling worktree with a unique branch and perform all
  edits, installs, and checks there.
- Never modify the primary checkout.
- Report the worktree path and branch when starting work in a dedicated worktree.

## Git history

- After completing and validating a task, commit its changes on the task's work
  branch without waiting for a separate request.
- Never commit directly on `main`.
- Keep Git history linear. Rebase feature branches onto the target branch and
  integrate changes with a fast-forward or squash; do not create merge commits.

## Development database migrations

- Keep schema changes in `db/migrations` as SQLx versioned `.up.sql` and
  `.down.sql` pairs. From the repository root, create a pair with
  `sqlx migrate add --source db/migrations --reversible <name>`.
- Keep applied migrations immutable. Add a new pair for each schema change;
  do not fold changes into the baseline or put manual schema scripts in
  `db/upgrades`.
- From the repository root, apply migrations with
  `sqlx migrate run --config sqlx.toml --source db/migrations`, inspect them with
  `sqlx migrate info --config sqlx.toml --source db/migrations`, and revert the
  latest version with
  `sqlx migrate revert --config sqlx.toml --source db/migrations`.
  Commands read the root `.env`; set `DATABASE_URL` to select another database.
- SQLx owns each migration transaction. Do not add `BEGIN` or `COMMIT` to the
  migration files. Keep each down migration limited to its up migration's changes.
- Test forward upgrades with existing records and the full down/up cycle in an
  isolated database. Preserve imported data when upgrading an existing database.
- The one-time transition from the consolidated baseline requires schema and
  data verification before aligning its checksum. Follow `db/README.md`;
  changing the checksum alone does not apply schema changes.

</INSTRUCTIONS>

# Production scorer contracts and verification

## Overview

The scorer replaces one outbound adapter. `DeclarationResolverService::resolve_declarations` reads checked cleaned evidence, builds `ScoringInput`, calls `FunderScorer::score`, applies `ResolvedDeclarations::from_scored`, then publishes the complete output. Identity and payment attribution remain domain policy. No database is involved in clean or resolve.

## Contracts and flow

- `domain/repositories/declaration_resolution.rs` owns the async `FunderScorer` port. It returns `ScoredPairs` or `EntityIngestionError` and must report actual model/runtime provenance.
- `domain/models/declaration_resolution/input.rs` groups normalized name and optional address into sorted profiles, unions their blocking keys, and stores observation membership internally. Repeated profiles with an unresolved observation get a `-repeat` row so they can be compared statistically. `needs_resolution` is true when any profile member lacks a company anchor. Profiles with only anchored members need no statistical link to one another. Do not change this shaping when replacing the adapter.

It does not prove candidate completeness, blocking correctness, calibration, or truth of provenance. Those are scorer obligations. Retain this final check.
- `outbound/declaration_resolution.rs::SplinkScorer` currently serializes input into temporary files, invokes Python in `spawn_blocking`, checks output protocol and frozen model/runtime keys, then calls `ScoredPairs::checked`. Replace subprocess/runtime validation with native inference and typed configuration/provenance. Use the existing `EntityIngestionError::DataError` pattern for native errors and join failures.
- `inbound/cli.rs` constructs storage and scorer from `DeclarationResolverConfig`, then passes budget separately to the service. Current config requires Python executable, defaults worker path and budget, and validates positive budget. Remove Python fields and worker defaults. Keep the native config's own invalid values visible at construction rather than silently repairing them.
- `domain/models/declaration_resolution.rs::ResolvedDeclarations::from_scored` calls identity policy, independently attributes payments, and writes `scored.model` into manifest `model`. The manifest also records package/policy versions, cleaned input digests, profile and output counts, threshold and budget. `outbound/declaration_loading.rs` checks manifest schema/policy, digests and counts but does not inspect scorer-specific model fields. Typed native provenance can serialize at this existing JSON boundary without schema changes.

## Candidate budget

The budget limits both distinct profile candidates and distinct expanded observation decisions. Current Python counts the entire OR blocking join before predicting and refuses excess. It predicts with threshold zero, checks returned count against candidate count, and sorts keys. Native generation must deduplicate all rule matches, preserve every generated candidate below budget and refuse excess before an unbounded candidate collection. `ScoredPairs::checked` is a post-materialization safety check, not sufficient allocation protection. An adapter may keep at most budget plus a refusal sentinel while enumerating, or perform bounded/counting traversal before materialization. A library API that creates the full candidate collection before returning cannot satisfy this contract by checking its length afterward.

`identity.rs::expanded_edges` skips self observation pairs and pairs with two company anchors, canonicalizes endpoints, deduplicates a BTreeMap and rejects at budget + 1. Keep this second, independently bounded expansion. An implementation must never truncate either collection.

The five frozen rules all require `left.needs_resolution OR right.needs_resolution`: exact name, exact nonnull address, equal first three Unicode characters, first-character plus two-character final ASCII-word prefix with left-only suffix exclusion, and overlapping domain blocking keys. The suffix regex is `[a-z]+$`, and its empty match remains an empty string. Its excluded suffix list is applied only to the lexicographically left profile. Union and dedup must preserve that asymmetry. Blocking keys include normalized aliases and the special Unite trade-union key; they are not a new generic tokenizer.

The previous raw schema already stored both `member_id` as UTF8 UUID and `parliament_member_id` as UInt32. A scratch-only conversion therefore needs no database identity lookup. Read each old partition, require one nonzero Parliament source ID throughout it and a consistent old UUID, then write a fresh partition named `<parliament_member_id>.parquet` with the old `member_id` column removed. Preserve every other field, row, type, nullability, timestamp and source_json. Reject duplicate destination IDs rather than overwrite or blindly concatenate. Preserve an audit map of old partition UUID to source ID. Verify the actual old Arrow schema and per-partition IDs before conversion; this grounding established the old schema from source history, not by decoding retained parquet.

Place converted raw at `<scratch-data-root>/<retained-ingestion-key>/raw/declarations`, with no cleaned/resolved output copied. Resolve uses a separate native config with the same scratch root/key and an explicit sufficient budget. Do not run fetch or load. Keep the original directory read-only and never publish outputs there.

The CLI currently lacks an old-format importer or an output-root override for clean, so conversion and copying to scratch happen before the CLI. This is verification preparation, not a production backward compatibility requirement. `raw/members.parquet` is unnecessary for clean/resolve because each declaration partition supplies its source member ID.

Run-level local identity IDs depend on the lexicographically first observation in a component, so compare component membership after this mapping rather than require identical provisional ID strings. Preserve the ingestion key to avoid adding another namespace difference.

Compare the native candidate pairs, gamma levels, probabilities, expanded decisions, canonical components and payment attribution against the independent old-Splink reference after this mapping. Inspect freshly published manifest and parquet counts/digests. Verify refusal on insufficient budget produces no resolved directory. # Codex tool mapping for pstack

## Tool actions

| pstack / Claude action | Codex equivalent |
|------------------------|------------------|
| Read a file | `shell` (`cat`, `head`, `tail`) |
| Create / edit / delete a file | `apply_patch` |
| Run a shell command | `shell` |
| Search file contents / find files | `shell` (`rg`, `grep`, `find`, `ls`) |
| Fetch a URL | `shell` with `curl` / `wget` |
| Search the web | `web_search` |
| Invoke a skill (the `Skill` tool, `/command`) | Skills load natively. Follow the instructions presented. |
| Dispatch a subagent (the `Agent`/`Task` tool) | `spawn_agent` |
| Dispatch N parallel subagents in one turn | N `spawn_agent` calls in one response |
| Wait for a subagent result | `wait_agent` |

# Rust domain development

Apply the [repository coding policy](../../../AGENTS.md). Choose the representation
that enforces the required behavior before adding implementation logic.

## Find the owner

Name the incoming data shape, the valid domain states, and the invariant the
change must preserve. Find the existing type that owns that rule. Search its
callers and serialized spellings before creating another representation.

Trace a changed domain type through its producer, encoder, decoder, service,
and persistence mapping. Change the affected consumers in the same task.

## Choose the representation

- Use an enum for a closed vocabulary. Share its serialization and deserialization
  definition across producers and consumers. When a separately versioned external
  contract needs its own type, convert it explicitly into the canonical domain
  type at the boundary.
- Represent mutually exclusive states with an enum carrying the fields each
  state requires. Use newtypes for identifiers with different meanings and
  checked constructors for values whose validity depends on runtime facts.
- Use exhaustive matches without a fallback when variants require different
  behavior. Adding a variant must require a decision at those matches. Do not
  add artificial matches when every variant already supports the same operation.
- Keep transport DTOs only where the external shape differs from the domain
  shape. Their domain-bearing fields still use the canonical types. Reuse an
  existing result record when it already defines the serialized contract.

## Parse at the boundary

Decode external values into domain types before passing them to services.
Reject unknown labels during parsing. Do not parse a domain enum into a string
and then reconstruct its vocabulary with a membership check.

Keep checks for runtime facts such as duplicate IDs, missing references,
artifact digests, and stored timestamps at the responsible boundary. Types
cannot establish facts about files or database rows that have not been read.
Propagate the existing error types instead of hiding failures with defaults.

Keep domain decisions in the domain model and transaction ownership in the
repository. Convert typed values into storage representations at the persistence
boundary using the canonical encoding. Preserve existing service abstractions.

## Fix the structure

When a failure reveals two owners for one rule, identify the canonical owner and
delete the competing definition. Updating both copies leaves the cause intact.
Stay within the affected contract rather than expanding into unrelated cleanup.

In Exposed, the resolution domain owns `IdentityBasis`, `PairReason`, and the
attribution decision types in
[`declaration_resolution.rs`](../../../exposed/src/lib/domain/models/declaration_resolution.rs).
The [declaration loader](../../../exposed/src/lib/outbound/declaration_loading.rs)
must decode those types. It must not maintain a second list of accepted labels.
This applies to other finite domain vocabularies too.

## Verify the contract

Run the relevant behavior checks and the real entry point affected by the change.
For serialized contracts, verify that producer output is readable by the consumer
and that malformed external values are rejected. Preserve the intended wire
format, supported versions, and persistence behavior unless the task changes them.

Check the compiler guarantee directly when the task relies on it. For example,
temporarily add a variant to confirm the semantic matches reject missing handling,
then revert the probe. A passing runtime test does not prove exhaustiveness.

Run formatting and applicable compiler or lint checks. Distinguish diagnostics
introduced by the change from existing failures. Report which invalid state the
types now exclude and which runtime checks remain necessary.

# Rust domain development

Apply the [repository coding policy](../../../AGENTS.md). Choose the representation
that enforces the required behavior before adding implementation logic.

## Find the owner

Name the incoming data shape, the valid domain states, and the invariant the
change must preserve. Find the existing type that owns that rule. Search its
callers and serialized spellings before creating another representation.

Trace a changed domain type through its producer, encoder, decoder, service,
and persistence mapping. Change the affected consumers in the same task.

## Choose the representation

- Use an enum for a closed vocabulary. Share its serialization and deserialization
  definition across producers and consumers. When a separately versioned external
  contract needs its own type, convert it explicitly into the canonical domain
  type at the boundary.
- Represent mutually exclusive states with an enum carrying the fields each
  state requires. Use newtypes for identifiers with different meanings and
  checked constructors for values whose validity depends on runtime facts.
- Use exhaustive matches without a fallback when variants require different
  behavior. Adding a variant must require a decision at those matches. Do not
  add artificial matches when every variant already supports the same operation.
- Keep transport DTOs only where the external shape differs from the domain
  shape. Their domain-bearing fields still use the canonical types. Reuse an
  existing result record when it already defines the serialized contract.

## Parse at the boundary

Decode external values into domain types before passing them to services.
Reject unknown labels during parsing. Do not parse a domain enum into a string
and then reconstruct its vocabulary with a membership check.

Keep checks for runtime facts such as duplicate IDs, missing references,
artifact digests, and stored timestamps at the responsible boundary. Types
cannot establish facts about files or database rows that have not been read.
Propagate the existing error types instead of hiding failures with defaults.

Keep domain decisions in the domain model and transaction ownership in the
repository. Convert typed values into storage representations at the persistence
boundary using the canonical encoding. Preserve existing service abstractions.

## Fix the structure

When a failure reveals two owners for one rule, identify the canonical owner and
delete the competing definition. Updating both copies leaves the cause intact.
Stay within the affected contract rather than expanding into unrelated cleanup.

In Exposed, the resolution domain owns `IdentityBasis`, `PairReason`, and the
attribution decision types in
[`declaration_resolution.rs`](../../../exposed/src/lib/domain/models/declaration_resolution.rs).
The [declaration loader](../../../exposed/src/lib/outbound/declaration_loading.rs)
must decode those types. It must not maintain a second list of accepted labels.
This applies to other finite domain vocabularies too.

## Verify the contract

Run the relevant behavior checks and the real entry point affected by the change.
For serialized contracts, verify that producer output is readable by the consumer
and that malformed external values are rejected. Preserve the intended wire
format, supported versions, and persistence behavior unless the task changes them.

Check the compiler guarantee directly when the task relies on it. For example,
temporarily add a variant to confirm the semantic matches reject missing handling,
then revert the probe. A passing runtime test does not prove exhaustiveness.

Run formatting and applicable compiler or lint checks. Distinguish diagnostics
introduced by the change from existing failures. Report which invalid state the
types now exclude and which runtime checks remain necessary.
